newsitem.title: ITALY: Anti-trust launches fresh Telecom Italia probe.
newsitem.headline: Anti-trust launches fresh Telecom Italia probe.

text.p: Italy's anti-trust authority said on Tuesday it was launching an investigation into complaints that Telecom Italia was abusing its dominant market position and stifling competition.

The authority said in a statement that rival firm Albacom had accused the state controlled Telecom Italia of blocking access to circuits which would allow the creation of dedicated phone networks for business clients.
"In addition Telecom Italia would seem to be renting direct circuits for a much higher price than that seen in major European countries," the anti-trust said.
"This has the effect of hindering the offer of new telecommunications services by competing companies," it added.
Albacom, which is owned by Banca Nazionale del Lavoro British Telecom and Mediaset, sells telecom services for closed user groups.
It is the second time within two months that the watchdog body, headed by former prime minister Giuliano Amato, has opened an inquiry into Telecom.

Last November it probed complaints that the state company had been offering discounts of up to 30 percent for domestic and international traffic but had denied the discounts to Albacom. A ruling is still awaited.
The anti-trust said on Tuesday that Albacom was now also complaining that when dedicated networks were made available, they were charged much more for the service than other Telecom clients.
Telecom Italia was not immediately available for comment. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
